CLIMATE CATASTROPHE: ASSUME THE WORST To Wake Up, And Mitigate It Complacency kills agency, and agency is most human. Humanity can set changes in motion that it cannot subsequently govern. In particular with the climate. A little computation in the present essay suggests that, beyond 4 degree Celsius of heating, the DOMINANT contribution to heating will be a natural feedback caused by WATER VAPOR. This is a rough, that is a philosophical approach, a simple idea, what physicists call a “back of the envelope calculation”. But that simplicity makes it all the more hard to contradict and powerful. Vested interests of the corrupt experts of the dominant, hydrocarbon elite, explain why that computation has not been revealed, and was not made public before. The gravest danger may therefore lie beyond the emissions we produce directly: warming can awaken other sources of warming, from thawing permafrost to changes in water vapour, while disrupting oceans, ice and living systems. None of this establishes that a catastrophic chain reaction is inevitable. It does mean that uncertainty about its limits should sharpen our response, rather than soothe us. The immense carbon store in frozen soils illustrates both the danger and the need for care: releasing much of it is an illuminating thought experiment, not a forecast. Its potential effect on warming is formidable; its direct effect on atmospheric oxygen is comparatively small… But significant! Meanwhile, billions of people reasonably seek more energy and greater comfort. Asking them to remain poor and destitute while plutocrats and their servants cavort around the planet, cannot be a climate strategy (although it could incite a well deserved revolution). We need abundant carbon-free energy, vigorous fundamental research, and the capacity to act if dangerous feedbacks emerge. Prudence requires taking the worst possibilities seriously enough to prevent them. *** The worst case for climate evolution under human forcing is not just a return to Jurassic conditions (+ 10 C), but an uncontrollable run-away greenhouse, the ultimate case of an amplifying feedback . (In the present United Nations scientific predictions, neither of these situations is viewed as a possibility… I want to point out in the present essay that this exclusion is wrong and unwise…) By “runaway greenhouse” we mean complete loss of human control over the climate, a worst case scenario than the return of the Jurassic. Humanity risks becoming a volcanic eruption unto itself… By spewing GreenHouse Gases (GHG) onto itself as no volcano has since the Dekkan Traps (they were part of the complex Cretaceous extinction mechanism). By “run-away”, we do not mean “Venus-like”. Earth has plate tectonics which buries carbon and surface rocks which absorb it [1]. It is not as far-fetched as it sounds: it has long been suspected that the impact(s) which helped bring the end of the dinosaurs brought a worldwide thermal shock. Giant volcanic events, also characterized by enormous CO2 emissions, Large Volcanic Provinces, 250 and 66 million years ago, brought worldwide cataclysms. The worst possibility with man-made global heating is devastating NONLINEAR FEEDBACK HEATING LOOPS, from the unleashing of natural chain reactions. Historical examples of naturally occurring disasters of a nonlinear character which accompanied, for thousands of years after the end of the last great glaciation are legions: The three Dryas instant mini glaciations (Younger Dryas, etc..) , each a millennium long, were named after an Arctic flower. Those Dryas episodes were highly counter-intuitive; they are now understood as shut downs of the Gulf Stream, which is part of the world’s most significant oceanic current. Repetitive giant floods, erupting sea floor from huge eruptions of caged methane (“clathrates”) causing tsunamis, have also occurred etc., In the early Nineteenth Century, the evolutionists Lamarck and Cuvier confronted each other, sometimes bitterly: Lamarck believed in constant biological evolution, Cuvier held evolutions happened by catastrophes. It turned out that they were both right. Catastrophes were legions in evolution. The Permian–Triassic extinction , about 252 million years ago , eliminated roughly 90% of all species. Large Igneous Province in Siberia. . How could nonlinear feedback loops of similar violence arise nowadays? Well, worse, much worse could happen. One has to realize that we are engaged in the most brutal thermal and CO2 shock for at least three million years . Overall, several indicators, such as sea level, are not as high as in the Eemian, 110,000 years ago, the last great interglacial warm period… But the CAUSAL indicators, such as the CO2 equivalent density, are much higher than in the Eemian. There has been enough heating in the Arctic (+ 4C) for natural nonlinear effects to get launched: permafrost melts, liberating CO2 and CH4. Those nonlinear effects have been observed. They will get much worse in the future because it is likely that the burning of hydrocarbons will increase in the near future. The fundamental geopolitical reason for this further rise in hydrocarbon usage is that most of the world does not use enough energy to feel comfortable enough. And that is without even counting the new needs of AI (US AI companies intend to solve this by locating AI in space and sourcing solar energy there; Google just launched the first satellite to implement this; other countries may not have as easy access to space). *** VIRTUE DISPLAYING INEFFECTIVE ECOLOGY; THE SORRY CASE OF FRANCE: The paradigm of aborting ecology is saintly France, the church of woke, the crashing and depressing martyr of the green ineffective ecological crusade . As of September 2026, the French deficit is at 5.5% and the French short term interest rates are higher than Greece’s. The country, long the world’s industrial and technological leader, during the Middle Ages, and main author of US independence, has deindustrialized to a fatal level and is adrift . This devastating situation has greatly been caused by far pseudo-left and maniacal pseudo-ecology and self-destructive do-goodism (example: two perfectly well functioning nuclear reactors were closed to please Germany; meanwhile French nuclear electricity is offered to other European countries below cost, jacking up the price France pays). The latest official estimate puts French 2024 consumption based greenhouse gas footprint at 8.2 tonnes of CO₂ equivalent per person , against 5.4 to 5.9 tonnes for emissions on French territory alone (sources differ slightly). The difference between 5.9 and 8.2 is called China. Indeed, France achieved those noble numbers by pushing all its industry underneath a green carpet. France sent most of the industry France had 30 years ago… to China (more exactly ⅔; France industrial GDP went from 20% of total GDP down to 7%; Italy and Germany kept their 20%…). In truth the average French emits thirty percent more CO2 per year if French bound Chinese production is taken into account. Even then France has the highest ratio of nuclear power to GDP in the world. As the world CO2 average is 4 tons, this means that, just to raise to the French comfort level, CO2 emissions, worldwide, need to be more than doubled. We will prevent that legitimate demand to turn into a disaster only if we develop and deploy a new energy source without carbon. That could be forms of fission-fusion nuclear energy, or maybe even space solar. China has already developed 250 Gigawatt of solar panels, as of 2026, the equivalent of at least 50 large nuclear reactors, but China is a bit of a special case: China has dependable desert sun but also the high voltage lines to carry electricity from desert to coastal cities (thanks to its authoritarian government). Few countries have this combination. For energy 24/7, non-carbon, only nuclear fission is available right now (wind will probably turn long term into a costly mistake in most sites). In other words, we need to accelerate energy research considerably. This is the safest avenue to avoid a runaway GHG crisis. Just the opposite of the anti-progressive pseudo-ecologists’ credo of no development. *** WATER VAPOUR IS A VERY POWERFUL GREENHOUSE GAS . NASA estimates that water vapour and clouds together account for roughly 75% of the present natural greenhouse effect . So here comes a nonlinear amplification: as air warms, its capacity to hold water vapour rises by roughly 7% per °C , and that extra vapour traps more heat. How much more trapping of infrared from water vapor than from CO2? If temperature rose 5C, by how much would the greenhouse effect augment? Each additional degree of global warming allows roughly 7% more atmospheric water vapour. That extra vapour adds approximately 1.5–2 W/m² of greenhouse trapping; allowing for the accompanying change in atmospheric temperature profile leaves a net amplification of about 1.3 W/m² per degree. Now there is only about 2.2 W/m² of additional radiative forcing from CO₂ since 1880. CO₂’s ~2.2 W/m² helped drive a temperature rise of ~1.5°C, and that rise includes amplification by H₂O. *** INCREASING WATER VAPOR WILL MAKE SOON A VERY NICE CATASTROPHE: Suppose Earth goes to + 5C (we are at + 1.5 C, maybe +2C). Say we got there by doubling the CO2 and overall GHG, plus water vapor feedback. So we have say 5 Watts per square meter from this combination. Then, at that point, +5C, the H2O vapor would force at (1.3) (5) = 6.5 Watts per square meter… So H20 forcing would dominate the GHG forcing! The nonlinear water vapor feedback would indeed exceed the initiating GHG forcing . That is a powerful amplification. More subtle considerations at this point could be engaged, nuancing our rough estimate: increased infrared radiation from the planet’s surface, effects on clouds (which may diminish), etc. But the following fact remains: around twice the present warming already suffered, water vapor infrared trapping will start to dominate whatever humanity is emitting, we will enter a run away regime … *** PERMAFROST GIANT CARBON STORE, READY TO BURST: On our way to get steamed by water vapor, we may get some help from a huge unknown, the permafrost . It’s failing spectacularly in high mountain ranges. But most of it, up to a mile deep , is located in regions which are warming the fastest. As permafrost melts, it releases CH4, methane, with 80 times the heating power of CO2 (over the first twenty years)..It can even explode, in formidable detonation, sometimes thirty meters across and one hundred meters deep (OK, especially in places with lots of CH4, my point entirely…) If one considers that there is 1,600 billion tonnes of carbon stored in permafrost soil , an all-released thought experiment gives a very large result. If every atom of that carbon becomes CO₂ and stays in the atmosphere , NOAA’s conversion of 2.12 billion tonnes of carbon per 1 ppm CO₂ gives: Difference CO2 = 1600/2.12 = 755 ppm… Adding to the present 425 ppm CO2, one gets around 1200 ppm. However, using the conversion factor for the equivalence into general GreenHouse Gazes, one goes up to around 1800 ppm… Thus the possibility of a nonlinear feedback loop, a chain reaction of global heating exists. Computations, in the worst case scenario, show an impact on oxygen production, especially as oxygen making organisms are dying from the increasing oceanic heat, all over the planet. *** So here is the permafrost computation. I did it more than 15 years ago and French president Macron seems to have used it in a discourse in Brazil, and that was intensely criticized (and may have led a Brazilian president to darkly evoke a future war with France) One knows the total oxygen content in the atmosphere. It’s 10^18 kg (one million billion tons). One can assume, in the case of a run away greenhouse, the death of blue green bacteria from ocean heating and forests from fire, droughts, infestations. So no more oxygen production. Then one computes how much mass of permafrost there is . . Permafrost stores roughly 1,600 billion tonnes of carbon, chiefly as frozen, incompletely decomposed organic matter. Thaw permits microbes to turn some of it into CO₂ and methane; methane subsequently oxidizes, consuming atmospheric oxygen as it becomes CO₂. Methane that oxidizes completely consumes atmospheric oxygen: CH4+2 O2⟶CO2+2 H2O Thus one tonne of methane consumes four tonnes of O₂ . Moreover,: oxygen consumption is not unique to methane . Aerobic decay of the original organic matter also consumes oxygen. Methane formation can postpone part of that consumption until the methane oxidizes in the atmosphere. So we must not count both the decay of a given piece of carbon and the later oxidation of its methane as two complete, independent oxygen demands. As a deliberately impossible upper-bound illustration, converting all 1,600 billion tonnes of stored carbon into CO₂ by simple carbon oxidation would require about 4,300 billion tonnes of O₂ . That is consequential chemistry, but only roughly 0.3–0.4% of the atmosphere’s oxygen reservoir ; real release would involve only a fraction of the stock and would occur over time. The immediate danger is the extra greenhouse warming , while oxygen loss is a distinct question requiring a rate and an atmospheric oxygen budget. *** IS THERE MORE THAN 1600 BILLION TONS PERMAFROST? CONSIDER BATAGAY: I made the following evaluation: if we liquefied all of the planet’s oxygen contained in the atmosphere we would get a worldwide layer of two meters (from the total mass of 10^18 kg of oxygen). Now it is said that the total carbon in permafrost is 1600 billion tons, corresponding to a worldwide layer of 3.5 centimeters of carbon over the 18.7 million square kilometers of permafrost regions. Combined the latter with the former, to get a diminution of oxygen of .4% after oxidation. There is a giant slide in Siberia, the Batagay slide, with a 55 meters cliff. A 2024 study estimates that Batagay has put in motion 169,500 tonnes of organic carbon within 34.7 million m³ of ground and ice since it formed. That works out to about 4.9 kg of carbon per cubic metre of sliding material . At that concentration, a hypothetical 55 m column would hold about 270 kg C/m² , equivalent to about 12 cm of graphite —several times the supposed 3.5 cm average. Some will point out with glee that the 3.5 cm is just an average. Yes, but Batagay is also a spectacular case, and it’s not obvious that it’s not the case pretty much everywhere like that all over Siberia. Moreover there is probably even more carbon below the slide. The point is that a bit of thinking shows the alternance of hard glaciations and warm periods in the last three millions years may have constituted a carbon making machine short-circuiting the usual disposal of carbon in the deep ocean. Now this is just a speculation on my part, but why not? Experts paid by an oil tyranny will find it difficult to persuade me that their main expertise is not simply in pleasing their masters. . The widely cited 1,600-billion-tonne inventory is not a ceiling. Sparse sampling of deep Siberian deposits leaves the size of any additional carbon reservoir uncertain. Sources report permafrost reaching about 1,500 metres in parts of Siberia. Imagine that. How did it form? Glaciation alternating with warm periods over three million years may have piled up immense amounts of carbon. But do not expect experts paid by the hydrocarbon tyrants who rule Russia to tell you an alarming truth. *** GLOBAL HEATING → DROP OXYGEN 1.37 mm of graphite spread over the whole Earth. The reaction C+O2→CO2 consumes 32 kg of O₂ for every 12 kg of carbon . The 1,600-billion-tonne carbon MINIMUM scenario consumes about 7 mm of oxygen , a little over one-third of 1%. My proposed larger carbon inventory would scale this proportionally: four times the carbon would consume about 29 mm of liquid oxygen, or 1.4% of the atmospheric O₂ stock. Under the assumption that oxygen producing species had disappeared that would correspond to a gain of altitude of 125 meters. No big deal. However: *** HEAT UP THE OCEAN, EXTRACT MOST OF THE OXYGEN: Broad open-ocean oxygen minimum zones arise largely because sinking organic matter is decomposed, consuming oxygen, while oceanic circulation replenishes that slowly from the depths. Oxygen poor regions existed before modern human warming. Humans intensify them: warmer water holds less oxygen, and changes in mixing and circulation can reduce the supply reaching subsurface waters Global oceans have lost about 2% of their dissolved oxygen in the period 1960-2017 due to ocean warming and nutrient pollution, threatening marine life and ecosystems Between 0 C and 40 C, oceanic water loses half of its dissolved oxygen (total oxygen in the ocean is two-third of one percent of total oxygen content in the atmosphere…). The Super El Nino occurring in 2026-27 is supposed to bring up ocean temperatures in the upper layers (100 meters or more). That basically brings the oxygen content of sea water down by 10%. Now imagine a future hyper El Nino, and the temps go up 10C: 20% oxygen reduction. It is known that during intense warming, hundreds of thousands of years ago, El Nino happened every year. *** EXPERT CORRUPTION BY HYDROCARBON POWERS THAT BE: Most Very Serious People will scoff that a run away greenhouse could never happen. Many of these deriders are experts of the IPCC/GIEC who have to be taken very seriously, all the more as The Guardian identified 20 cases of strong potential conflicts of interest among 223 Working Group III lead authors , 11 of them Saudi-linked .(ARAMCO, etc.). That’s nearly 9% of 223 lead authors, and The Guardian is no doubt aware that there are many other hydrocarbon establishments, worldwide. Indeed the IPCC talks mostly about secondary problems. The resulting dissolved ions are carried to the ocean, where they precipitate as carbonate minerals. This process removes CO₂ from the atmosphere–ocean system on timescales of 10⁵–10⁶ years and strengthens as temperatures rise (warmer, wetter conditions accelerate weathering). This carbonate–silicate cycle feedback helped keep Earth’s climate within a habitable range for billions of years. Plate tectonics (carbon burial and recycling) Oceanic plates subduct carbon-bearing sediments inside oceanic crust into the mantle. Some of that carbon is returned via arc volcanism and mid-ocean-ridge degassing, but a substantial fraction is stored in the deep Earth or continental lithosphere over geologic time. Continuous plate motion also refreshes the supply of fresh silicate minerals available for weathering, preventing the system from becoming “supply-limited.” However, these mechanisms operate far too slowly to counteract century-scale anthropogenic emissions (although actively breaking and exposing fractal silicate mafic rocks has been considered as a quick way to lower CO2; by Gigatons per year, an added benefit is that powered rock could be used as a crop nutrient; it would require much energy, though, so we are back to square one: to lower CO2, new energy is required) *** [2]. Acero y disipadores elevan capacidad sísmica de edificios en la Cdmx El acero y los disipadores de energía permiten mejorar la capacidad lateral y de deformación de edificios ante sismos, según análisis de Gerdau Corsa. Por Deyanira Vázquez | Reportera En la Ciudad de México, el uso de acero estructural combinado con sistemas de disipación de energía puede incrementar la capacidad de edificios para responder ante movimientos sísmicos, de acuerdo con un análisis técnico de Gerdau Corsa sobre dos inmuebles ubicados en la zona de lago de la capital. El estudio “Uso de disipadores de energía en edificaciones de acero” evaluó los edificios de Sinaloa 95, en la colonia Roma Norte, y Ámsterdam 219, en la colonia Hipódromo. En ambos casos, las alternativas con sistemas de protección sísmica mostraron incrementos en la resistencia lateral y la capacidad de deformación respecto de las soluciones estructurales originales. Los resultados adquieren relevancia debido a las características del subsuelo de distintas zonas de la ciudad de México, particularmente aquellas asentadas sobre antiguos depósitos lacustres, donde las condiciones del terreno pueden amplificar los efectos de un movimiento sísmico. El análisis de Gerdau Corsa toma como referencia los daños registrados durante el sismo del 19 de septiembre de 2017. Disipadores modifican la respuesta de los edificios Uno de los casos corresponde al inmueble de ocho niveles y semisótano ubicado en Sinaloa 95. Para este proyecto se analizó la incorporación de 64 disipadores de energía tipo Dampo BRB, dispositivos que utilizan un núcleo de acero y un comportamiento no lineal para disipar parte de la energía generada durante un movimiento sísmico. Frente a la solución estructural original, el análisis reportó un incremento de hasta 36% en la capacidad lateral de la estructura y de 74% en su capacidad de deformación. Las simulaciones también registraron demandas promedio inferiores a 35% de la capacidad de deformación considerada en el sistema. El segundo inmueble, localizado en Ámsterdam 219, presentó una configuración estructural más irregular. La alternativa estudiada sustituyó parte de la solución original de concreto por marcos de acero y añadió 72 disipadores Dampo BRB y 24 disipadores viscosos. De acuerdo con el estudio, esta configuración permitió incrementar hasta 114% la capacidad lateral y 109% la capacidad de deformación frente a la propuesta estructural original. El análisis también reportó menores desplazamientos laterales y distorsiones máximas de entrepiso en las soluciones con protección sísmica. El acero permite soluciones de protección sísmica Rigoberto Torres, jefe de Asistencia Técnica de Gerdau Corsa , señaló que la ductilidad constituye una de las propiedades relevantes del acero para el diseño de estructuras sometidas a acciones sísmicas, debido a que permite considerar deformaciones importantes antes de alcanzar una falla. La posibilidad de combinar marcos, contraventeos y dispositivos de disipación permite adaptar las soluciones estructurales a las condiciones de cada proyecto. Gerdau Corsa señala que los contraventeos restringidos al pandeo, utilizados como disipadores histeréticos, son una de las alternativas empleadas para mejorar el comportamiento de edificaciones ante acciones sísmicas. Además del comportamiento estructural, el acero puede modificar los procesos de construcción. La fabricación previa de componentes permite transportar elementos terminados al sitio y realizar posteriormente el montaje, una característica que puede resultar útil en predios con restricciones de espacio y alta actividad urbana. –sn– Acero ¡Conéctate con Sociedad Noticias ! El radón es un elemento químico perteneciente al grupo de los gases nobles. En su forma gaseosa es incoloro, inodoro e insípido y en forma sólida su color es rojizo. En la tabla periódica tiene el número 86 y símbolo Rn. Su masa media es de 222, lo que implica que por término medio tiene 222-86 = 136 neutrones. Igualmente, en estado neutro le corresponde tener el mismo número de electrones que de protones, esto es, 86. Es un elemento radiactivo y gaseoso, encuadrado dentro de los llamados gases nobles. El radón es producto de la desintegración del radio (226Ra), elemento altamente radiactivo. El isótopo 219Rn es producto de la desintegración del actinio, llamado actinón y tiene una semivida de 4 segundos. Además de todos estos, el radón tiene 22 isótopos artificiales, producidos por reacciones nucleares por transmutación artificial en ciclotrones y aceleradores lineales. El isótopo más estable es el 222Rn, también el más abundante, con una semivida de 3,8 días y producto de la desintegración del 226Ra. Al emitir partículas alfa se convierte en 218Po. Aplicaciones: La emanación del radón del suelo varía con el tipo de suelo y con el contenido de uranio superficial, así que las concentraciones al aire libre del radón se pueden utilizar para seguir masas de aire en un grado limitado. Este hecho ha sido puesto al uso por algunos científicos atmosféricos. Aunque algunos médicos creyeron una vez que el radón se puede utilizar terapéuticamente, no hay evidencia para esta creencia y el radón no está actualmente en uso médico, por lo menos en el mundo desarrollado. When Technology Goes Wrong: The Most Famous Accidents in History Archival and illustrative depictions of major technological failures throughout history—from maritime and industrial disasters to nuclear meltdowns—that reshaped modern safety standards. Dear Cherubs, some of history’s most famous disasters began with something remarkably ordinary: a collision, a faulty valve, a calculation, a storm, or someone thinking, “That should probably be fine.” Spoiler: occasionally, it very much was not. THE ACCIDENTS THAT CHANGED HISTORY Take the Titanic in 1912. Nearly 2,200 people were aboard when the supposedly unsinkable liner struck an iceberg; roughly three-quarters of those aboard died. The disaster became one of the defining maritime accidents of the modern era and helped drive changes in international maritime safety. According to NOAA, its impact was amplified by the way wireless communication allowed the tragedy to unfold in the public eye almost in real time. Five years later came the Halifax Explosion. Two ships collided in Halifax Harbour, including the French munitions carrier Mont-Blanc, which was carrying explosives. The resulting blast killed about 2,000 people, injured thousands more and destroyed or damaged huge parts of the city. Parks Canada describes it as the largest human-made explosion before the atomic bomb. Then there are industrial accidents where the technology itself becomes the villain. Bhopal, India, in 1984, saw a toxic gas release from a pesticide plant. The exact death toll remains disputed, but the World Health Organization records thousands of immediate deaths and many more long-term health consequences. It remains one of the most consequential industrial disasters ever recorded. Chernobyl followed in 1986. A failed safety test at Reactor 4 resulted in an explosion and fire and the largest uncontrolled radioactive release in the history of civil nuclear power. The numbers surrounding its long-term health effects are complicated, because confirmed deaths, projected radiation-related deaths and deaths from other causes are not the same thing. WHO estimates that up to around 4,000 eventual radiation-related deaths could occur among the most highly exposed populations. WHEN ONE MISTAKE BECOMES A LESSON Not every famous accident kills thousands. Britain’s Buncefield explosion in 2005 caused enormous destruction when a fuel-storage tank overflowed and a vapour cloud ignited. More than 40 people were injured, but remarkably nobody died. The UK Health and Safety Executive subsequently investigated the causes and introduced safety changes affecting major-hazard industries. Fukushima in 2011 shows another category: a natural disaster triggering a technological one. The earthquake and tsunami disabled power and cooling systems at Fukushima Daiichi, causing three reactor cores to largely melt. NOAA records more than 15,900 deaths from the wider Great East Japan earthquake and tsunami disaster as of March 2026, while the nuclear accident itself must be considered separately from the enormous natural disaster surrounding it. The uncomfortable lesson is that “accident” rarely means one thing simply went wrong. Usually, several small failures, assumptions or unfortunate circumstances line up at exactly the wrong moment. And that may be the most useful thing about studying these disasters. We cannot undo them, but we can learn why they happened. Humanity has spent centuries discovering, often painfully, that technology is brilliant right up until somebody forgets to check the backup system.
